chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fishing of the Magians when they strike with the net and do not recite a name, or the Jews and do not recite a name. He said: There is no objection. Indeed, the fishing of fish is merely catching them.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible
key_terms.وَلَا يُسَمُّونَ: And they do not recite a name

ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by Magians or Jews without reciting a name permissible to eat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the fish caught by Magians and Jews is permissible (*halal*) because the act of extraction itself constitutes the slaughter, rendering the recitation of a specific name unnecessary. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that for fish, the mere act of catching or removing it from water is sufficient for permissibility, distinguishing it from land animals which require specific slaughter rites. The narration underscores the practical ease in dietary laws regarding non-Muslims' catch, provided the method does not involve prohibited elements.
